title: First return in sequential machine composition
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $M_1,M_2$ be deterministic $k$-work-tape machines over Boolean symbols, with state sets $S_1,S_2$ and a decidable equality on $S_1$. Choose an exit state $e\in S_1$, an entry state $u\in S_2$, initial state $s\in S_1$, final state $q\in S_2$, three families of $k$ Boolean work-tape words $w_0,w_1,w_2$, and times $T_1,T_2\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $M_1$, started in state $s$ with tape words $w_0$, reaches the configuration with state $e$ and words $w_1$ at time $T_1$, and does not have state $e$ at any earlier time. Suppose also that $M_2$, started in state $u$ with words $w_1$, reaches state $q$ and words $w_2$ at time $T_2$, and does not have state $q$ at any earlier time. Then the machine formed by switching from $M_1$ at state $e$ to $M_2$ at state $u$ does not reach state $q$ in its $S_2$ component at any time $t<T_1+1+T_2$ when started from state $s$ with words $w_0$.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1$ reaches the configuration with state $e$ and words $w_1$ at time $T_1$
$M_1$ has not reached state $e$ at any time before $T_1$
$M_2$ reaches the configuration with state $q$ and words $w_2$ at time $T_2$
$M_2$ has not reached state $q$ at any time before $T_2$
